:JUDGMENT:
The Claim Petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. Brief facts of the Petition are as under:
That on 25.08.2020 at about 5.00 a.m., on Kolar-Bengaluru - NH-75, near Chikkanahalli Gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, while the petitioner was proceeding on his Honda Shine Motor-cycle bearing no.KA-05-JC-5432, a Goods Tempo bearing no.KA-51-A-5364 was parked in the middle of the road unmindfully without exhibiting any indicators, parking lights or any signal; the petitioner who could not notice the said lorry due to high-beam light emitted by vehicles coming from opposite-direction, could not avoid dashing his Motor-cycle against the said parked-lorry.
As a result, the petitioner fell-down and sustained grievous-injuries.

That immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Srinivasa Speciality Hospital, Hosakote, and then to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar,
where he was treated as an inpatient from 25.08.2020 to 26.08.2020.

entities.text: Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
That the petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards Medical treatment,
Nourishment, Conveyance and Attendant charges.
3. That prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as an Accountant in LG Service Center, earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, the petitioner has sustained grievous-injuries leading to permanent disability.
4. That Respondent no.1 is the Owner and Respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the offending-vehicle and both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to Petitioner.
Hence this Petition.

5. In pursuance of notice, Respondent no.2-Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed its objections to the main petition; whereas, Respondent no.1 remained absent and has been placed exparte.
6. In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.2-Insurer has denied the age, avocation, income of the Petitioner and also that the accident was due to the rash and negligent parking of the Goods Tempo.
It is contended that the driver of the Goods Tempo had no valid driving licence to drive the vehicle, and the Goods Tempo had no valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

Also, that the accident was due to the negligence of the petitioner who was riding the vehicle without valid,
effective driving licence.
That the petitioner was solely responsible for the alleged accident.
Respondent no.2 has thus prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed:

sentences.text: ISSUES

1 . Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 25-08-2020 at about 5.00 a.m., near Chikkanahalli Gate,
on Kolar-Bengaluru NH-75 road, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru, due to negligent parking of Goods Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-02-ME- 5958 in the middle of the road without exhibiting indicators, parking light or any signal?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award ?
8. In support of his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as PW.1 and has got marked Exs.P.1 to 9; a witness has been examined as PW.2 and Exs.P.10 to 13 have been marked.
On the other hand, Respondent no.2 has got 4 witnesses examined as RW.1 to 4 and Exs.R.1 to 10 have been marked.
9. Perused the materials on record.
Heard both-sides.

10. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :
Issue No.1:
It is the case of petitioner that he has sustained grievous-injuries in the accident caused by the driver of the offending Goods Tempo bearing no.KA-51-A-5364.

Per contra,
respondent no.2 has denied that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Goods Tempo.
Respondent no.2 has contended that the offending Goods Tempo had no valid Permit as on the date of accident.
12. In support of his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as PW.1, a witness as PW.2; and has got marked 9 documents.
Ex. P-1

to Ex.P-6 are the True copy of FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar,
IMV Report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex. P.7 - 2 Discharge Summaries.
Ex . P.8
is the notarized-copy of Aadhar card of Petitioner, Ex.
P.9 - 23 Medical Bills.

13. A perusal of FIR & Complaint at Exs.P.1 & 2 shows that, Nandagudi Police have registered the FIR against the driver of the offending Goods Tempo bearing no.KA-51-A-5364 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC on the complaint lodged by the Petitioner; the accident Anandappa M. 3 has taken place on 25.08.2020, whereas the complaint has been lodged on 28.08.2020.

sentences.text: Thus there is delay of about 3 days in filing the complaint.
14. Next, Ex.P.3 shows that the concerned Police have conducted the Mahazar at the accident spot.

However, it is relevant to note that the petitioner has not produced the 'Spot Sketch' to know the exact spot on the road where the offending Goods Tempo was parked and the accident has taken-place, so as to come to a conclusion as to whose 'negligence' has led to the accident.
15. Next, it is relevant to note that the petitioner has not produced the MLC & Police Intimation.
On the contrary, Respondent no.2 has got 4 witnesses examined as RWs.1 to 4 and Exs.R.1 to 10 have been marked.
The Official of RTO has been examined as RW.1 who has clearly deposed that the offending Goods Tempo bearing no.KA-51-A-5364 had valid Permit as on the date of accident on 25.08.2020.
Initially Respondent no.2 had contended that the offending vehicle had no valid Permit, but the evidence of RW.1 clarified this aspect.
The Senior Manager of the Employer of petitioner has been examined as RW.2 who has produced Exs.R.3 to 7 viz., Salary Slips from April 2020 to August 2020.
The MRO of Srinivas Hospital, Hosakote, has been examined as RW.3 who has produced Exs.R.8 to 10 viz., Authorization Letter, Police Intimation & MLC respectively.

The Investigation Officer (since Retired) has been examined as RW.4 who has deposed that he has not prepared the Spot Sketch in the case, and that the Spot Sketch is not usually prepared in Rural Police Stations.

In this way, the witnesses who were to be examined by the petitioner have been examined by respondent no.2.
16.
The Police Intimation & MLC at Exs.P.9 & 10 which are first in point of time thus prove the accident.

Next, as per the IMV Report at Ex.P.4: Damages to Petitioner's Motor-cycle: Front- wheel Mudguard, Head-light Assembly, Shock absorber forks are damaged, Crash-guard bent on left-side and Foot-gear shifter on left- side damaged; Damages to offending Tempo: the right-side rear wheel mud-guard of the Goods Tempo is shown to have been damaged.

Here, it would be apt to refer to the complaint at Ex.P.2:

.
But in the absence of Spot Sketch, it is not clear as to where exactly was the Goods Tempo parked.

However, the fact that the "right-side rear wheel mud-guard of the Goods Tempo has been damaged, is indicative of the fact that it had not been parked on the middle of the road; because had it been parked on the middle of the road, the left-side rear-end of the Goods Tempo would have been damaged.

Thus this fact not only shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the Goods Tempo who had Anandappa M. Alias Ananda vs Bajarangi Transport on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9437129/
4 parked the vehicle without without exhibiting any indicators, parking lights or any signal, but also the negligence of the petitioner who failed to notice the Goods Tempo parked by the side of the road.

sentences.text: The petitioner could have averted the accident had he been slow and cautious/not negligent; on the other hand, had the driver of the offending Goods Tempo not been negligent and had exercised caution by exhibiting the indicators, parking lights or any signal, the accident would not have taken-place.
In this way, there is negligence on the part of both the riders.
The learned counsel for petitioner has argued that there is no 'contributory negligence' on the part of the petitioner.

In this regard, the learned counsel has relied-on the decisions reported in :
1. 2024 ACJ 2019 (SC) (CA No.2659 of 2024 decided on 19.02.2024) between Radha Rani and others Vs. Mohar Singh and another.
2. 2024 ACJ 2161 (SC) (CA No.10648 of 2024 and others ;
decided on 19.09.2024) between Sushma Vs. Nitin Ganapati Rangole and others.

The above referred decisions are not applicable to the case on hand, since in these decisions, it has been proved that the offending vehicles had been parked 'dangerously' on the 'middle of the road'
without any indication.
As already discussed above, here it is not proved that the offending Tempo was parked on the 'middle of the road'.
Under the circumstances, the 'contributory negligence' on the part of the petitioner can be held to be to an extent of 20%.
17. Next, the I.O has filed the charge-sheet at Ex.P6 against the driver of offending Goods Tempo and it has remained unchallenged.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is due to the rash and negligent driving by the petitioner as well as by the driver of the offending Goods Tempo, in which the petitioner has sustained grievous-injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Partly in the Affirmative".
18. Issue No.2:-
Having proved that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Goods Tempo, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

19. As per the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.5 issued by Srinivasa Hospital, the petitioner has sustained "cut lacerated wound over anterior aspect of left thigh; Bone protruding through it, bleeding and fracture of shaft of left femur".
The petitioner has examined the Doctor of Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar, who has treated him as PW.2 and Exs

Ex.P.10 is the Recent Clinical Examination Notes, Ex.P.11 is the Disability Assessment Form &
Evaluation, Ex.P.12 is the Inpatient Record, and 8 - X-Rays are at Ex.P.13.

PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner had been admitted and discharged twice; that the fracture has united and the implants have been removed; and that he has not furnished documents pertaining to follow-up treatment of petitioner.
He has assessed the disability of left lower-limb of the petitioner at 45% and whole body disability at 15%.
Thus as per the evidence of PW.2, the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner has affected left lower limb, and the whole body disability is assessed at 15%.

But Anandappa M. Alias Ananda vs Bajarangi Transport on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9437129/

sentences.text: 20. Next, in the petition, the age of the petitioner is shown as 26 years; in all the Medical documents, his age is shown as 28 years, and in the Aadhar card of petitioner at Ex.P.8, the age of petitioner is shown as 25 years.
The age of 26 years shown in the petition is regarded as petitioner's age.
Also, as per the petition, the petitioner was an Accountant in LG Service Center and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But it is respondent no.2 who has examined the Senior Manager of the Employer of petitioner as RW.2 who has produced Exs.R.3 to 7 viz., Salary Slips from April 2020 to August 2020.
However, the I.T.Returns are not on record.
Hence the average of the net-pay shown in the salary-slips at Exs.R.3 to 7 which comes to about Rs.15,000/- is considered as petitioner's income.
21. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the petitioner who is aged about 26 years is '17'.
With multiplier of 17, income of Rs.15,000/- per month and the whole-body disability of Petitioner at 10%.

The future loss of income works out at: Rs.15,000 X 12 X 17 X 12/100 = Rs.3,67,200/- and the petitioner is entitled for the same as compensation under the Head 'Future loss of income'.
22.

The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he has been treated as an inpatient at Sri Gaurav Hospital from 25.08.2020 to 31.08.2020 for surgery, and at R.L.Jalappa Hospital - from 26.10.2023 to 27.10.2023 for the removal of implants.
Owing to the nature of injuries sustained, the petitioner has undergone Pain, Shock & Suffering.

He is thus entitled for Anandappa M. Alias Ananda vs Bajarangi Transport on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9437129/
6 compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards 'Pain, Shock and Suffering'.

sentences.text: The petitioner having lost the usual comfort of life due to the injuries sustained, is entitled for a sum of Rs.25,000/- under the Head 'Loss of Amenities'.
Further, the petitioner might have laid-up for atleast 2 months due to multiple-fractures.

Thus considering the laid-up period as 2 months, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- (@ Rs.15,000/- per month) under the head 'Loss of income during the Laid-up period'.
23.
Admittedly, during the laid-up period of 2 months, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and might have spent some amount towards extra diet, nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/-
(Rs.10,000/- x 2) towards Attendant's charges, Extra Diet and Nourishment and Conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards the Head.
24. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards Medical-expenses.

He has produced 23 Medical bills at Ex.P.9 amounting Rs.1,08,380/- Among them, the Inpatient Medical Bill at Sl.No.1 of Ex.P.9 which is for a sum of Rs.78,300/-and the Inpatient Bill for Rs.2130/- and OP Bill for Rs.2320/- at S.No.16 & 17 of Ex.P.9
are the only acceptable Medical Bills; the other bills are of the period during treatment and are also without Prescriptions.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.82,750/- as compensation under the Head Medical Expenses.

25. Considering the above aspects, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation as under :
1. Future Loss of Income Rs.3,67,200/-
2. Pain & Suffering Rs. 40,000/-
3. Loss of Amenities Rs. 25,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid-up Rs. 30,000/-
period 5. Food, Nourishment, Rs. 20,000/-
 Conveyance and Attendant  Charges 6. Medical Expenses Rs. 82,750/-

Thus the petitioner is eligible for compensation of Anandappa M. Alias Ananda vs Bajarangi Transport on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9437129/
7 Rs.5,65,000/- (rounded-off)

sentences.text: But as already discussed in Issue no.1, there is contributory-negligence on the part of petitioner to an extent of 20%.
Hence on deduction of 20% towards Contributory negligence i.e., Rs.1,13,000/- out of the eligible compensation of Rs.5,65,000/-, the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,52,000/-
The petitioner is thus entitled to Rs.4,52,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
26. Regarding Liability :
As already discussed above, the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Goods Tempo bearing KA-51-A- 5364.
And there is no dispute regarding the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending-vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents no.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, respondent no.2 being the insurer has to indemnify the insured, and it has to deposit the compensation amount with interest.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

27. Issue No.3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.4,52,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 30 days from the date of the Award.

Out of the award amount, 50% is ordered to be released to Petitioner by way of E-Payment after proper identification, and the remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
